title: A holiday gift: The success story of Hampstead Hill Academy
summary: Education news can feel like a diet of doom and gloom, but there are success stories that are a gift to the students who attend them, writes Kalman Hettleman, who points to Baltimore's high-performing, odds-beating Hampstead Hill Academy.
content:
by Kalman Hettleman, Maryland Matters December 23, 2025

by Kalman Hettleman, Maryland Matters December 23, 2025

You wouldn’t know it from daily news across the nation, state and city, but many schools are beating the odds and achieving outstanding results. They are all a gift to our schoolchildren.

It’s not easy to single one out, but I am particularly in touch with the Hampstead Hill Academy, a neighborhood K-8 school up the street from where I lived in the Canton area of Baltimore City. It’s a shiny holiday ornament: Proof that a school predominantly serving students from low-income backgrounds and students of color can succeed at high rates.

Here are some facts and figures.

Student achievement. Hampstead Hill is the only city school to earn a 5-star (highest) ranking in the 2025 state report cards. It ranks 16th in middle schools and top 25 in elementary schools statewide.

It has the highest test scores overall in  the city, with 63.9% of  students achieving proficiency on at least one of the state tests. It topped second place Baltimore Polytechnic Institute (my alma mater) with 60.7%.

On the Maryland State Department of Education school report cards.  Hampstead Hill is the highest performing city elementary or middle school based on academic, school quality and student success measures.

On absenteeism. Hampstead Hill’s chronic absentee rate of around 9% is well below the state  average of around 30% and city schools’ average of around 49%.   Its daily attendance rate of 95% substantially exceeds the overall rates for both the city and state.

On measures of family satisfaction. An unpublished report indicates overall family satisfaction was 96% compared to 83% for all city schools

So what is Hampstead Hill’s secret sauce? There are many tangible and intangible factors but here are a top five.

Many other schools have some or all of these ingredients (except the family roots). So, if we know a secret sauce, how do we get it cooking in other schools in the city and elsewhere?

Not easily. My overriding impression is that the success factors at Hampstead Hill are not all that dramatically different from familiar school improvement strategies; rather, it’s that they’re executed at a higher level. One lesson is that school systems must pay more attention to effective implementation of instructional and school climate best practices.

Hornbeck says we’re “doing what works well,” with some innovative add-ons. In particular, he cites their “restorative practices” program which builds relationships and healthy communication among students, teachers and parents.

Whatever the exact Hampstead Hill gift package, we should celebrate the extraordinary dedication of all public school educators. They are year-in and year-out blessings.

Happy Holidays to all!
